hypothesis.claim: A streaming HSP1 input boundary can supply exactly one repeated Endpoint428 Q16 pretruth row for every HARM-Delta predictive GSRT2 coordinate, bind raw/WRT/coder and optional physical-source evidence, reproduce the frozen source fixture with exact P/K identity, and reject every declared coverage, ordering, probability-domain, repeat, scope, and provenance corruption without reading corpus data.
hypothesis.falsification: Reject this ABI if the valid fixture does not replay identically, if sparse coverage or P/K identity fails, if opening G becomes admissible without a physical tape, if a valid physical tape cannot be bound, if any declared corruption escapes, if source identity drifts, or if any corpus path is opened.

changedMechanism: Add a zero-credit streaming sparse-parent and physical-seed input envelope around the already frozen HARM-Delta callback adapter; do not change its route, donor, edit, mixture, control, scope, or update semantics.
invariants: The HARM-Delta static contract has SHA-256 2a2b37a2a32bf6115a9f4c8e68cd8b45f18cc6f8869b1f638c328d8e59454a42.
The HARM-Delta source binding has SHA-256 e20bf8d95cd37ea767f0ebe1b8d9c8efa0d8e9546852cf93439ab5e9e8df24ba and every artifact listed inside it must verify before import.
HSP1 coordinates are strictly increasing and cover every and only the parent-provider calls made by the replayed predictive GSRT2 population.
Every HSP1 row contains eight Q16 P1 counts in [1,65535] and is consumed before the corresponding truth byte updates HARM state.
GSRT2, HSP1, and any HGS1 physical-seed stream are independently materialized A/B inputs with exact byte identity.
The manifest binds canonical raw, WRT, coder-bit, frontend-state, parent-state, mapping, source, and observer identities without granting correctness to opaque mapping or state receipts.
A distant manifest must contain a nonempty repeated HGS1 stream and produce an admissible G comparator; opening and fixture manifests require G to remain inadmissible.
This gate generates its own eight-byte source fixture, cannot open a compressor or canonical corpus, and has zero score or gain authority.
No corpus-bound HARM or PALIMPSEST replay is authorized before the active HORIZON experiment terminalizes through its fail-closed router.

controls.definition: Valid generated WRT, GSRT2-A, HSP1-A, mapping, source binding, and scope manifest replay.
Separately materialized GSRT2-B and HSP1-B inputs must be byte-identical to A and produce the identical replay and terminal state.

Ten frozen mutations cover repeat drift, missing/extra/duplicate sparse rows, zero probability, payload-hash drift, source-binding drift, physical-observer drift, and scope arithmetic drift; every mutation must be rejected.
The fixture has no physical seed stream, so G must remain asleep and inadmissible rather than becoming a free zero comparator.

population.selection: A fixed generated two-occurrence explicit template-field fixture; no canonical corpus, active parent trace, or partial scientific result is opened.
population.coordinate: Zero-based WRT byte, MSB-first coder bit, and equal generated raw coordinate in [0,8).
